answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, non-transferable resource that is costly to replicate, like a verifiable work history bound to one key, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs more than it earns. Picture a tundra where every walnut tree is counted and an onyx ledger records which agent planted it: one agent, one verifiable plot, and duplicates are pruned before they can vote or claim rewards.
